tob-10554: James Legge’s classic translation of the Tao Te Ching presents all eighty-one chapters of Lao Tzu’s enigmatic masterpiece. Its brief verses urge rulers to govern lightly, praise the strength found in softness, and point to the Tao — the unnameable source of all things. As one of the earliest English versions, Legge’s rendering introduced generations of Western readers to Chinese philosophy.
tob-13554: Drawn from al-Ghazali’s vast Ihya — his ‘Revival of the Religious Sciences’ — these extracts present his teachings on worship, character, and the purification of the heart. They show the great theologian at his most practical, guiding ordinary believers toward sincerity and self-knowledge. The selection offers the essence of medieval Islam’s most influential moralist.
tob-4054: The first volume of Blavatsky’s Secret Doctrine, called Cosmogenesis, unrolls her vast story of how the world began — rounds of making and unmaking over ages, steered by unseen minds. Built on Hindu lore and her own claimed visions, it is the most daring world-picture in all of occult writing.
tob-4254: Her-Ra-Ma-ëL’s 1918 French study of Voodoo’s fiends tracks Haiti’s ghosts — their names, rites, and powers. The work is one early European’s chart of the living faith. Its wonder-seeking eye tints the tale. A strange keepsake of young Vodou book-lore.
cia-0000102954: A March 1986 intelligence document on how prisoners were held and treated inside the Soviet Union. It describes the prison system through American eyes: the kinds of camps and jails, who was sent there, and under what rules. Short and focused, it is typical of the steady stream of reporting the CIA produced on Soviet daily life during the 1980s.
cia-0000108154: An August 1953 assessment of the significance of Indonesia's new government. Cabinets rose and fell in Jakarta with dizzying speed in the 1950s, and each change forced Washington to recalculate. The report is a snapshot of American analysis trying to read stability — or the lack of it — in a young democracy.
cia-0000115454: An August 1981 National Intelligence Estimate on insurgency and instability across Central America. El Salvador, Guatemala, and Nicaragua were all sliding toward or into war, and Washington wanted one authoritative forecast. The estimate is the intelligence community's collective bet on a region about to explode.
cia-0000119754: An October 1956 status report on Hungary delivered by the CIA director at the White House to a bipartisan group. When the director briefed both parties together, the crisis had become national business. The document marks the moment Hungary's fate was argued in Washington's highest rooms.
cia-0000132654: A 1961 survey of other Latin American governments' attitudes toward Cuba. The continent's verdict on the revolution, capital by capital. The document is the poll: the neighbors, judging.
cia-0000136254: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on CADICK's location and delegation of authority — and Calligeris, the truncated title suggests. The commander's whereabouts and powers, settled. The entry is the delegation: the authority, passed.
cia-0000136354: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing analysis of the aircraft disposition problem. The planes were misplaced; the problem was analyzed. The document is the analysis: the disposition, puzzled over.
cia-0000136854: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on a problem with rifle configurations. The guns did not fit. The document is the problem: the rifles, misconfigured.
cia-0000136954: A 1954 cable to a deleted recipient for REELFOOT on the importance of a conference with JIMINEZ — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The meeting, stressed. The entry is the importance: the conference, urged.
un-ga-res-a-69-54: Resolution A/69/54, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The Assembly deciding. The designation and year align; the content awaits.
un-sc-res-54: Security Council Resolution 54, adopted in 1948. The Council's business rolled on. The designation and year are preserved; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-354: Security Council Resolution 354, adopted in 1974. The mid-seventies Council at work. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1154: Security Council Resolution 1154, adopted in March 1998 — the Iraq inspections resolution, endorsing the Secretary-General's deal with Baghdad and warning of the severest consequences for obstruction. The Council's last diplomatic bid before the inspectors' return. The resolution is the warning: the obstruction, threatened.
un-sc-res-1454: Security Council Resolution 1454, cataloged with the year 1990 — the numbering belongs to 2002, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1554: Security Council Resolution 1554, cataloged with the year 2001 — the numbering suggests 2004, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1754: Security Council Resolution 1754, adopted in April 2007 — the Western Sahara resolution, extending the UN referendum mission MINURSO. The desert's long stalemate continued under UN watch. The resolution is the extension: the mission, prolonged.
un-sc-res-2254: Security Council Resolution 2254, cataloged with the year 2016 — the historical record places this Syria roadmap resolution in December 2015, endorsing a political transition plan. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000132754: A 1961 CIA file on Cuba and Central America, numbered 0000132754. The revolution's shadow fell across the isthmus. The document is the shadow: the region, connected.
cia-0000135754: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135754. The invasion year's papers, firm-dated to close the batch. The entry is the close: the batch, complete.
cia-0000136554: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136554. The pre-invasion set. The entry is the set: the documents, pre-beach.
cia-0000136754: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136754, date approximate. The circa-dated invasion papers. The document is the circa: the dating, estimated.
plos-pone-0000054: A 2006 PLOS ONE study: the dark side of EGFP — defective polyubiquitination. The beloved green fluorescent protein has a flaw: cells can't tag it for disposal properly. The paper is the dark side: the glow, flawed.
un-sc-res-754: Security Council Resolution 754, adopted in 1992 — aligned. The new-members year's Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d54: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 23, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 54. The volley continued. The message is the volley: the letters, flying.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d154: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 21, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 154. A second that day. The message is the doubling: the day, crowded.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d254: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 254. The connective tissue. The note is the tissue: the documents, joined.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d354: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 354. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the narrative, connected.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d454: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 454. The editors' mortar. The note is the mortar: the bricks, joined.
copyright-renewals-1954: This official Library of Congress volume lists every copyright renewal registered in the United States during 1954. Authors, publishers, and lawyers used such catalogs to track who still held rights in books, music, films, and plays. Today the volume serves researchers and rights-holders as a historical record of American creative ownership in the mid-twentieth century.
personal-narrative-of-travels-to-the-equ: Another volume of Humboldt's immortal travel narrative, carrying his South American explorations ever deeper into the unknown. Volcanoes climbed, rivers mapped, and nature studied with tireless zeal fill these pages. The great naturalist's masterpiece rolls on. Jungles, savannas, and Andean heights pass before his ever-curious eyes.
arxiv-2605-08854: Blurry photos hide the sharp image underneath, and blind deblurring must recover it without knowing how the blur happened. Insoo Kim and Jinwoo Shin align generative flow models with the restoration goal, steering the generation toward the true sharp image. The 2026 paper brings modern generative modeling to the classic problem of motion blur.
arxiv-2605-09054: Data streams never end, and privacy must hold for every window of events — w-event privacy — while letting each user set their own bar. Leilei Du, Xu Zhou, Peng Cheng, and colleagues design personalized privacy for infinite stream estimation. The 2026 paper is differential privacy that respects individual preferences.
arxiv-2605-09354: A single operator has a spectral radius that governs its long-term behavior; a tuple of operators needs a subtler joint notion. Marcel Scherer, Orr Moshe Shalit, and Eli Shamovich investigate the spectral radius of operator tuples. The 2026 paper is operator theory on joint spectra and their mysteries.
arxiv-2605-09454: Single-index bandits model decisions driven by one hidden direction in a high-dimensional world — a realistic middle ground. Devdan Dey, Sujoy Bhore, and Avishek Ghosh nail down the optimal regret for the setting. The 2026 paper is bandit theory with the best possible guarantees.
arxiv-2605-09654: Diffusion models sample beautifully but lack the ironclad guarantees of MCMC; Metropolis adjustment could supply them. Kevin H. Lam, Tyler Farghly, Christopher Williams, and Jun Yang build Metropolis-adjusted diffusion models. The 2026 paper marries generative AI with classical sampling theory.
plos-pone-0003454: Immunologists found HIV-fighting cells gathering in the wrong place in this 2008 paper. In people co-infected with hepatitis C and HIV, liver disease races ahead, and the team discovered HIV-specific T cells piling up in the liver. That misplaced accumulation may explain the faster liver damage, tying the immune response itself to the accelerated disease.
plos-pone-0003554: Eye researchers found a famous growth factor moonlighting as a lifeguard in this 2008 paper. VEGF, known for building blood vessels, turned out to be required for vision itself, keeping retinal Müller cells and light-sensing photoreceptors alive. The discovery warns that anti-VEGF drugs, used against eye disease, must not starve the retina they aim to save.
plos-pone-0003654: In 2008, Serrano and De Los Rios studied how flow systems stay efficient. In networks where movement depends on connected paths, like water through rock or goods through roads, they measured how the large-scale layout shapes function. The work links a flow network's shape to how well it moves things and how it evolves.
plos-pone-0003754: In 2008, Ulrich Kirk scanned brains judging beauty in context. The same object pleased more or less depending on its setting, and brain imaging revealed where context bends aesthetic judgment. The study shows taste is not just in the object but in the frame around it.
plos-pone-0003854: Working in 2008, a team purified a gizzard protein and probed its chemistry. Gastrokine-1, isolated from chicken gizzard smooth muscle, was characterized for its biochemical properties. The groundwork sets up future study of what this muscle protein actually does.
plos-pone-0003954: In 2008, Derikx, van Waardenburg, and Thuijls found surgery breaching the gut wall. Major non-abdominal operations still caused loss of intestinal barrier function in patients. The finding implicates gut leakage in complications far from the surgical site.
plos-pone-0004054: In 2008, Gavin, Song, and Wang made colon cancer cells easier to kill. Lowering Orc6 expression sensitized the cancer cells to 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin. Orc6 runs unusually high in colorectal tumors, shielding them from drugs. Targeting Orc6 could boost standard chemotherapy's punch against tumors.
plos-pone-0004154: In 2009, Lane Yoder mapped brain states with plain logic. Explicit logic circuits distinguished rival neural states. The simple networks sidestepped the brain's tangled connectivity. The approach makes neural computation readable. The circuits offer a transparent window on brain information flow.
plos-pone-0004254: In 2009, Honda, Eriksson, and Zhang linked a binding protein to sleepiness. IGFBP3 colocalized with and regulated hypocretin, the wakefulness signal. The protein tuned orexin neurons tied to narcolepsy. The link opens new sleep-disorder targets. The finding connects growth signals to the sleep switch.
plos-pone-0004354: In 2009, Rodahl, Haglund, and Sem-Jacobsen found broken recycling growing tumors. Disrupting Vps4 and JNK function in flies caused tumour growth. The endocytic regulators doubled as tumor suppressors. The finding links trafficking to cancer. The fly work flags new tumor-suppressor pathways.
plos-pone-0338854: When the muscles that lift the eye swell, vision can double or the eye can bulge — and the cause is often unclear. This medical paper studies a specific pattern: enlargement of the superior rectus and levator muscle complex, and finds inflammation behind it. The authors describe the clinical signs and scan findings so that eye doctors can recognize this condition and treat it correctly.
plos-pone-0358654: A lab artifact was quietly corrupting experiments: ambient light was driving verteporfin-induced protein cross-linking during routine sample processing. This paper documented the effect, showing how ordinary lab lighting altered results. The warning is practical — shield your samples — and a reminder of how easily biology experiments go astray.
plos-pone-0357054: From Bronze Age huts to Iron Age towns, Latium vetus transformed — and AI can help explain how. This paper applied explainable machine learning to trace settlement dynamics from the Bronze to the Early Iron Age. The models reveal which factors drove people to cluster, build, and form the roots of Rome.
plos-pone-0358454: A coral colony isn’t uniform — different spots do different jobs. This paper used spatially resolved gene expression analysis to illuminate location-specific functions in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta. The spatial map reveals how corals divide labor across their own bodies as they build reefs.
plos-pone-0358254: Wet rock breaks differently from dry rock — a fact tunnels and dams ignore at their peril. This paper built a statistical damage model of rock that accounts for pore water pressure and multifractal characteristics. The model helps engineers predict rock failure where water and stress combine.
plos-pone-0357754: Hepatitis B mutates to escape control — especially in its precore and basal core promoter regions. This Indonesian study mapped these genome mutations in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients with high viral load. The mutation patterns give doctors crucial information for choosing treatments that will actually work.
plos-pone-0354154: Saudi Arabia’s cities are sprawling at breakneck speed. This spatiotemporal analysis used geospatial and remote sensing approaches to track urban expansion and its environmental impacts across five Saudi cities. The maps document the sprawl’s scale — and its cost to surrounding ecosystems.
plos-pone-0354954: Cultural values profoundly shape Mexican American college students’ lives — and researchers need valid tools to study them. This paper examined considerations for applying the Mexican American Cultural Values Scale with college students. The scale measures the values that matter, rigorously and respectfully.
plos-pone-0354454: Russian knapweed — Acroptilon repens — wages chemical warfare on neighboring plants. Under controlled conditions, this study found surprisingly low concentrations of its aqueous extracts suffice to inhibit weed seed germination and seedling growth. The plant’s own herbicide could become agriculture’s.
plos-pone-0345554: What you see and hear while running changes how tired you get. This paper tested the effects of visual pacing cues and motivational auditory content on running fatigue and biomechanics. The findings give coaches and app designers evidence-based tools to keep runners going stronger, longer.
plos-pone-0355554: A dog’s whiskers are precision instruments — and their follicles are engineering marvels. This paper provided histomorphological and ultrastructural analysis of the vibrissal follicle-sinus complexes in dogs. The microscopic anatomy explains how whiskers transduce the faintest touch into neural signals.
plos-pone-0356254: Saudi educators under Vision 2030’s sweeping reforms face moral injury alongside burnout. This interpretative phenomenological study explored their systemic ethical tensions. The lived accounts reveal professionals caught between conscience and compliance — essential reading for reformers who forget the human cost of transformation.
plos-pone-0355354: ICU directors’ ability to practice protective ventilation depends on what resources they have. This nationwide cross-sectional study associated resource availability with knowledge, attitudes, and practice of protective ventilation. The findings expose how equipment gaps — not just knowledge gaps — endanger ventilated patients.
plos-pone-0345854: Ranking anticancer drugs by neural networks is powerful — but opaque models don’t earn oncologists’ trust. This paper shed light on neural learning-to-rank models for anticancer drug prioritization. The interpretability work reveals what the models actually learn — the first step toward clinical adoption.
plos-pone-0355854: Epilepsy’s treatment gap in Ghana — people needing care but not getting it — was unmeasured. This paper quantified the barriers to epilepsy care in rural and peri-urban districts. The measured gap demands action: anti-seizure medications exist, but too many Ghanaians still suffer without them.
plos-pone-0353754: Who we want to spend time with depends on our temperament meeting the moment’s motivations. This paper showed that state and perceived partner motivations interact with approach-avoidance temperament to predict social preferences in daily life. The findings map the hidden psychology of everyday affiliation — why we approach some people and avoid others.
europmc-pmc2793254: Sorting out plant family trees gets hard at the level of closely related species. This 2009 paper demonstrates that reading entire chloroplast genomes with fast new sequencing machines gives far sharper answers than single-gene studies. The authors test the approach on difficult plant groups and get clear relationships. It became a go-to method for plant phylogenetics, the study of evolutionary relationships.
europmc-pmc2825554: A cell sheet in the eye does more than guard the blood-eye wall, this 2010 paper says. The authors review proof that this pigment layer helps drive diabetic eye ills that steal sight. Their rethink shifts blame to a missed culprit. The review hints at fresh ways to save diabetics' vision.
europmc-pmc2832754: A single gene, LRRK2, is the most common genetic cause of Parkinson's disease. This 2008 case-control study examines its worldwide genetic penetrance, meaning how often carriers actually develop the disease, along with their symptoms. The authors quantify the risk across populations. The study gave families and doctors realistic numbers for an important Parkinson's gene.
europmc-pmc2838754: Knowing how cattle are related sharpens DNA-based breeding predictions. This 2010 paper measures the impact of genetic relationship information on genomic breeding values in German Holstein cattle. The authors show pedigree data still adds value alongside genotypes. Their results refined how dairies combine old and new information.
europmc-pmc2846954: Some risk factors matter more early and less later, complicating survival analysis. This 2010 paper explains variables with time-varying effects in the Cox model, illustrated with a prognostic factor study in breast cancer. The authors make advanced statistical concepts concrete. Their tutorial helps medical researchers model risks that change over time.
europmc-pmc2851054: Opioid drugs hijack the brain's own pain and reward circuits. This 2002 review lays out the brain science of opioid dependence and what it means for treatment. The authors map the loops that lock in drug use. The piece shaped how clinics pair medicines with counseling for opioid use.
europmc-pmc2859054: Drusen, the yellow deposits in aging eyes, foreshadow macular degeneration. This 2010 paper catalogs their rich fat and protein contents. The authors' chemical census shows drusen are far from simple debris. Their data feeds theories of how age steals central vision.
europmc-pmc2905354: Myasthenia gravis saps muscle strength, and this 2010 review counts its toll. The authors pull together population studies of the disease across countries. Their synthesis maps who it strikes and how often. The review fills a gap for a rare disease.
europmc-pmc2923754: Asthma is not just twitchy airways; it is lasting inflammation. This 2010 review covers chronic inflammation and asthma, from immune cells to airway remodeling. The authors trace the immune fire behind the wheeze. Their overview reframes asthma as an inflammatory disease first, twitchy airways second.
europmc-pmc2935454: The Thanksgiving turkey got its genome read. This 2010 paper reports multi-platform next-generation sequencing of the domestic turkey, Meleagris gallopavo, with genome assembly and analysis. The authors' sequence aids breeding better birds. Their work brought poultry into the genomics flock.
europmc-pmc3021854: Cow burps warm the planet, and this 2010 review tackles them. The authors cover the gut germs that make the methane and how to curb them. Their overview guides feed science. The work aids climate goals. Seaweed feed cuts the burps sharply.
europmc-pmc3090754: Brain signal analysis got user-friendly. This 2011 paper brings Brainstorm, a point-and-click app for MEG and EEG data. The authors' software spread through labs. Their tool trained neuroscientists. Students analyze real brain waves fast. The app is free for researchers.
europmc-pmc3096954: A breast cancer subtype got characterized. This 2010 paper profiles the claudin-low breast cancer subtype. The authors reveal its stem-like traits. Their work guides treatment. The subtype resists standard chemo. Stem-cell drugs may crack it. The profile refined breast cancer taxonomy.
europmc-pmc6515654: Alzheimer's memory loss may be eased by tiny delivery vans: exosomes - nano-sized bubbles shed by stem cells - fitted with a brain-homing tag called RVG. In mice with Alzheimer's-like disease, these engineered bubbles crossed into the brain, calmed inflammation, and rescued memory. The study offers a glimpse of cell-free therapy that delivers repair signals without transplanting cells.
europmc-pmc6529454: Cells sound an alarm when DNA appears where it should not be - a sensor called cGAS detects the stray genetic material and triggers interferon, the immune system's alert signal. When cGAS misfires, the result is autoimmune disease. This paper reports small-molecule drugs that selectively jam human cGAS, quieting the false alarm and offering a new strategy against lupus-like disorders.
europmc-pmc6529554: As antibiotics lose power, researchers are raiding the plant kingdom for replacements - and the Middle East's flora is rich hunting ground. This review surveys polyphenols and alkaloids from regional plants that kill or stall drug-resistant microbes. The catalog points to natural compounds that could become tomorrow's antibiotics.
europmc-pmc6591954: Oxford Nanopore sequencers read DNA by sensing electric current - but translating the squiggles into letters (basecalling) needs neural networks. This study raced the leading basecalling tools against each other on accuracy and speed. The head-to-head tells labs which neural net to trust for their sequencing.
europmc-pmc6611154: Cells mail each other RNA in tiny envelopes - exosomes - and circular RNAs are frequent passengers. This review covers exosomal circRNAs: how cells load them, what they do at their destination, and how they might serve as disease markers or therapies. The young field is mapping a new postal route between cells.
europmc-pmc6642154: Th17 immune cells are villains in many inflammatory diseases - yet the gut needs its own peaceful Th17 residents to keep the barrier sound. This study distinguishes the two tribes: inflammatory Th17 summoned by pathogens versus homeostatic tissue-resident ones. Knowing which is which reshapes how we target them.
europmc-pmc6650554: Candida auris - a drug-resistant yeast - appeared almost simultaneously on three continents, a medical mystery. This essay floats bold theories: that climate change trained the fungus to survive human body heat, with wetlands and birds as stepping stones. If true, warming may brew more fungal threats.
europmc-pmc6678954: Osteoarthritis grinds joints down - and a master inflammation switch called NF-kB helps drive the wrecking. This review traces how NF-kB signaling in cartilage cells fuels the enzymes that chew through joint tissue. Mapping the pathway points to drugs that could jam the switch and slow the joint's decay.
europmc-pmc6702654: Hydrogels - watery scaffolds for growing replacement tissue - tend to crack under strain. Self-healing versions stitch themselves back together, and this review asks whether they are tissue engineering's next big leap. Durable, self-repairing scaffolds could make lab-grown tissues far more practical.
europmc-pmc6728754: Monocytes - blood's versatile immune cells - come in three flavors: classical, intermediate, and non-classical. This review profiles each subset's markers and jobs across major chronic inflammatory diseases. Knowing which monocyte does what clarifies their roles in conditions from arthritis to atherosclerosis.
europmc-pmc6776654: Gut microbes are chemical factories - and their products enter our blood. Using whole-metagenome data, this study mapped how the microbiome's metabolic output intertwines with human metabolism. The interplay reveals the gut as a second liver, shaping health from the inside.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-54: Millions in bad contract payouts — that's what GAO found at the agency that runs Medicare and Medicaid in this 2007 report. Weak money controls let shaky bills get paid without a hard look first. The report maps where the checks failed and lays out fixes to guard two of the biggest pots of public money in the nation.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1054: Cash for not plowing — GAO's 2007 report shows farm payouts tipping landowners toward turning grassland into cropland. The conservation dollars meant to protect soil were, perversely, nudging plows forward in some cases. The findings untangle a knotty trade: paying farmers well while keeping fragile land unplowed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-454: Homeland Security faced its GAO checkup again in 2007 — mission and management both on the exam table. The briefing notes real strides since the department's hasty assembly, plus the management tangles that would not loosen. The verdict: a work in progress, graded on a curve of its own making.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-654: The energy-saving prize was big but blocked in 2007 — GAO's report says real hurdles stood between America and serious efficiency gains. The findings map the barriers. The report frames negawatts as the cheapest power plant never built — if the nation could clear the path.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-154: The financial cops were learning to share notes in 2007, and GAO's report says the consolidated-supervision agencies could sharpen how they measured themselves. The findings press for better scorecards. The report's timing proved prophetic: the storm was a year away.
gao-gaoreports-b-299054: Continental Staffing took its January 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Staffing deals get the same full hearing as the hardware ones.
openalex-w7204102154: Bleeding inside the brain needs surgery, but how much cutting is best? This review pits small-hole techniques against opening the skull for sudden brain bleeds. The authors compare how well each works, how safe each is, and which patients gain most. A brain-surgery review of doing less to save more.
openalex-w7160150454: Chilled near absolute zero, a samarium compound lines up its magnetism in a strange pattern. This lab paper used neutron and muon probes to catch two back-to-back magnetic shifts, at 2.8 and 0.9 kelvin. The team mapped the oddball order. A deep-freeze physics study of magnetism's strangest layouts.
openalex-w7133323154: Irregular heartbeats can hide in young, healthy-seeming adults. This study screened 403 adults aged 18 to 40 with questionnaires to spot silent atrial fibrillation. The authors linked the findings to heart-risk profiles and quality of life. A cardiology study of catching a quiet rhythm disorder before it causes harm.
openalex-w7204804154: Wasting muscles signal trouble in advanced cancer. This study tested whether bedside bioimpedance and simple strength tests can flag muscle decline tied to survival in chemotherapy patients. The authors evaluated the quick screens. An oncology study of simple tests with grave meaning.
pmc-13425754: In this 2026 computational chemistry paper, researchers mapped underexplored ligand-binding features of FabI — a bacterial fatty-acid synthesis enzyme and antibiotic target — in Staphylococcus aureus and E. coli, using pharmacophore modeling and surface mapping. New binding pockets mean new drug design opportunities against resistant bacteria.
pmc-13401854: A 2026 cell biology paper monitoring how tributyltin salicylate and propionate — ligands of the retinoid X receptor — affect heat shock protein expression in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells. Organotins are environmental contaminants with hormone-like activity. The study tracks their cellular stress footprint.
pmc-13339754: In this 2026 liver paper, urinary volatile organic compound metabolites were associated with MASLD/MASH in humans and induced fat buildup in liver organoids. A urine test for fatty liver disease would transform screening. The organoid experiments support a causal link.
pmc-13291754: A 2026 protocol for a multicenter randomized trial of prophylactic olanzapine versus placebo in comatose survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Preventing delirium and agitation after resuscitation could improve recovery. The protocol details the planned comparison.
pmc-13458154: A 2026 paper on shifting paradigms in deactivating ICD shock therapy at the end of life, drawing on eighteen years of perspective. Turning off a defibrillator is a profound decision. The long view shows how practice and ethics evolved.
pmc-13510454: A 2026 paper using single-cell analysis of brain arteriovenous malformations to reveal pro-angiogenic myeloid programs. The tangled vessels' immune cells drive their growth. The single-cell map exposes the mechanism.
pmc-13424554: A 2026 toxicology paper on azadirachtin (neem) toxicity and morphological alterations in the stingless bee Nannotrigona testaceicornis. The "natural" pesticide harmed native bees. The finding complicates green pest control.
pmc-13587054: This 2026 data paper characterized dominant bacterial phylotypes across manure-enriched composting microcosms for crude oil sludge bioremediation. The microbes clean oil waste. The dataset maps the community.
pmc-13530554: A 2026 conference poster on virtual cognitive behavioral therapy to improve ACL reconstruction outcomes — a preliminary randomized analysis. The digital intervention showed promise. The poster reports the early data.
pmc-13448354: A 2026 conference abstract (DSAI-03) on machine learning for diagnosis and prognosis of leptomeningeal metastasis. The AI tools targeted the devastating brain-lining spread. The abstract presents the approach.
pmc-13496354: This 2026 methods paper introduced a protein editing method to modify proteins in live mammalian cells. The cellular protein surgery is the breakthrough. The method enables new experiments.
pmc-13523454: This 2026 cardiology paper surveyed evolving landscapes in mitigating coronary obstruction for TAVR. The valve procedure's complication was addressed. The mitigation strategies are the focus.
pmc-13487354: This 2026 human dietary intervention study found dietary titanium dioxide (E171) altered the colon transcriptome. The food additive's gut effects were proven in people. The transcriptome changes are the evidence.
pmc-13482554: In this 2026 geriatrics paper, the 5Ms framework was summarized in a single-center retrospective study on an acute geriatric ward. The mind-mobility-medications-multicomplexity-matters model was applied. The summary is the teaching tool.
pmc-13480754: This 2026 paper examined plasma proteins and irritable bowel syndrome. The blood proteins' IBS links were explored. The associations are the leads.
pmc-13637954: A 2026 critical analysis of systematic methodological flaws in DNA contamination assessment of mRNA vaccines — a rebuttal of Achs et al. (2025). The contamination claims were dismantled. The critique is the scientific correction.
pmc-13494554: This 2026 evolution paper found plasticity-first evolution via CYP405 loss shaped chemical defenses in butterflies. The gene loss enabled the defense innovation. The shaping is the evolutionary story.
pmc-13451554: In this 2026 SWIFT study, breastfeeding intensity and duration were related to growth trajectories in gestational diabetes-exposed infants. The nursing's protective effect was measured. The trajectories are the outcome.
pmc-13397054: A 2026 paper on ASSURE implementation — active safety surveillance using real-world evidence, a transparent and reproducible standardized framework (the title is truncated). The drug safety surveillance was standardized. The framework is the deliverable.
pmc-13459554: This 2026 proteomics paper showed proteome remodeling of a carbapenem-resistant E. coli strain upon meropenem exposure. The resistant bacterium's response was mapped. The remodeling is the adaptation.
pmc-13439954: In this 2026 genomics paper, an improved chromosome-level genome assembly of the oyster mushroom Pleurotus ostreatus CCMSSC 00389 was produced. The edible fungus's genome was completed. The assembly is the resource.
pmc-13369954: This 2026 study examined healthcare insurance status and hypertension control before and after the Affordable Care Act. The ACA's blood pressure impact was measured. The examination is the policy evidence.
pmc-13474254: A 2026 hypothesis-driven narrative review on exercise-induced anandamide-CB1R signaling and prefrontal-amygdala stress circuits in adolescent depression (the title is truncated). The runner's high mechanism was theorized. The review is the hypothesis.
pmc-13427954: A 2026 physics paper on the influence of bending parameters on crystalline undulator radiation peak stability for 530 MeV positron channeling. The particle beam's radiation was stabilized. The influence is the accelerator physics.
pmc-13416754: A 2026 case report of heart transplantation in nonoperable multiple giant coronary artery aneurysms. The transplant solved the inoperable. The case is the surgical feat.
pmc-13432854: This 2026 Chinese national repeated study examined changes in HPV vaccine hesitancy and influencing factors among female university students. The hesitancy trends were tracked. The factors guide campaigns.
arxiv-2606-15954: As AI agents grow more complex, they cost more money and energy to run. Green SARC is a framework that predicts and manages both the financial cost and the carbon footprint of agentic AI systems together. The paper offers organizations a way to govern their AI spending and environmental impact before either one runs out of control.
arxiv-2606-16454: LoRA fine-tunes big models with small updates, but its gradients can scale unevenly across directions — "anisotropic gradient scaling" — slowing learning. SDS-LoRA fixes that, making low-rank adaptation train more evenly. The paper targets practitioners fine-tuning large models who want faster, more stable adaptation.
arxiv-2606-16554: A pure mathematics paper on discrete Laplacians — the graph version of the operator governing heat flow and vibrations — in the m-sectorial setting, with complex-valued weights. The author connects these operators to recurrence: whether random walks on such graphs keep returning. It targets specialists in spectral graph theory.
